old: Loss of water gives a 2° cation next to the cyclobutane. A ring C–C bond migrates to the cation carbon, expanding the ring to a less strained cyclopentyl cation; that carbon now carries the CH3. A hydride shift (or direct loss of the H on the methyl-bearing carbon) then gives the trisubstituted ring alkene 1-methylcyclopentene.
new: Loss of water gives a 2° cation next to the cyclobutane. A ring C–C bond migrates to the cation carbon, expanding the ring to a less strained cyclopentyl cation: the former cation carbon (with its CH3) is now a ring carbon, and the positive charge sits on the neighboring former ring CH. A hydride shift (or direct loss of the H on the methyl-bearing carbon) then gives the trisubstituted ring alkene 1-methylcyclopentene.
why: Old wording implied the expanded cation sits on the methyl-bearing carbon; after the shift the charge is on the adjacent former ring carbon, which the following hydride-shift sentence already assumes.
